paragraphs: On Wednesday, Tom and Ben sat on the grass next to the school field. They were hot and tired after the football lesson. Tom drank some water from his bottle. "Do you prefer football or volleyball?" asked Tom. "I prefer volleyball," said Ben. "A volleyball team is smaller than a football team, so everyone plays more." "But football is more fun," said Tom. "A football field is much longer than a volleyball field." "Yes, but the net is very high," said Ben. "If the net is high, you must jump high."

"My dad likes golf," Ben said. "He plays on Sunday morning." "My dad thinks golf is slower than football." "It is not as fast as volleyball, is it?" asked Tom. "No, but it is very quiet," said Ben. Ben moved his arms like a golf player, and Tom laughed. "I like fast games," said Tom.

Then Coach Matt came across the field with a bag of balls. "Boys, I have good news," he said. "The university has a sports day on Saturday, and we can play volleyball there." "Do you want to come?" "Yes, please!" said Tom and Ben. "Where is the university?" asked Ben. "It is near, so we walk," said Coach Matt. "We meet at the school gate at eight o'clock."

"Turn right at the gate," said Coach Matt. "Walk through the park until you see a bridge." "Cross the bridge, and the university is on the left." "Right at the gate, through the park, over the bridge," said Tom. "The university is on the left, isn't it?" "Yes, that is right," said Coach Matt. "Please bring water and a hat."

Tom and Ben walked home through the park after school. They looked for the bridge. "It is there," said Ben. "On Saturday, I can show you how to hit the ball." "I prefer football," said Tom, "but I want to try volleyball."
